Filed a hole rather than an equivalent because the bytes genuinely differ on a reachable input.

verdicts.evidence: A clean --strict verdict already implies statuses.length > 0 for every category, so the conjunct cannot flip a status. Two code facts and one measurement: corpusDivergence (scaffold-lock.ts) makes any shipped rule that is absent or edited a strict gap, so a mission that can be clean carries a corpus that is a superset of the shipped 64; conformance() (conformance.ts:368-375) raises a violation for every CRITICAL/HIGH rule mapped to a gated phase with no manifest row; and measured on the shipped corpus 2026-08-27, each of the ten ASI categories is mapped by at least one CRITICAL/HIGH rule on a gated phase (thinnest: ASI05 and ASI07, one each). SENSITIVITY: the guard is load-bearing, not decorative - injecting a green verdict into a fresh mission's inputs (no manifest row anywhere) flips all ten controls partial -> `implemented`, which is exactly the paper-coverage asymmetry spec section 3 forbids. It is corpus DATA, not a code invariant, that keeps it unreachable: a future corpus leaving one category mapped only by MEDIUM/LOW or ungated rules makes this live again. Why it survived the net rather than why it is safe: the two unit tests over this branch supply no verdict at all (compliance.test.js:154, which is the paper-coverage case) or a green one on a mission whose rows exist, so neither reaches the combination, and the golden's fresh mission has a red gate.
